newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RUN NORWAY CLOSE IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RUN NORWAY CLOSE IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.

text.p: Hungary came close to causing an upset on Sunday when they outplayed Norway in the first half of a 1-1 draw in their World Cup European zone group three qualifier in Budapest's Peoples' Stadium.
Fresh from their 4-2 win over Brazil last week, the Norwegians, eight of whom played in the English premier league this season, were expected to overpower a Hungarian team short on experience.

"We were lucky to get one point," said Norway's manager Egil Olsen. "Hungary surprised us in the first half. They played better than I've seen them before and we were lucky not to concede more goals."

Olsen was more satisfied with the result than Hungarian coach Janos Csank, who before the match had indicated he would be satisfied with a draw but after 90 minutes felt his team should have taken all three points.
"Based on the picture of the first half, we should have won," he said. "I'm a little dissatisfied."

Norway could have gone ahead as early as the first minute when Tore Flo, put clean through by Stig Inge Bjorneby after just 34 seconds, side-footed past the right-hand post with only goalkeeper Gabor Babos to beat.

Norbert Nagy also wasted an opportunity for Hungary before Petter Rudi nudged Norway's nose in front after Babos could only palm out a long free kick by Henning Berg to Rudi, who volleyed the rebound in between two Hungarian defenders.

Hungary came back strongly and equalised through Zoltan Kovacs, who latched on to a delicate chip over the Norwegian defence by Hungary's man of the match, defender Emil Lorincz, to shoot powerfully past Frode Grodaas.

Hungary had several more chances in an exciting first half in which the Norwegian midfield, where Liverpool's four million pound signing Oyvind Leonhardsen failed to impress, ceded ground to the Hungarians, with Tamas Sandor and little winger Tibor Dombi tormenting a nervous Norway defence.

The frenetic pace subsided in the second half, although Frank Strandl's snap shot on the turn in the 56th minute whistled past Babos's post and Rudi brought out a fine double save from the Hungarian goalkeeper when he shot from 20 yards and followed up on the rebound.
For Hungary, Kovacs could have had a second when he overpowered Alf-Inge Haaland 40 yards out and darted forward to shoot straight at Grodaas.
"I think we played better on the second half and controlled it better in the second half but the Hungarians were good all the time," said Olsen.
The result keeps both teams in the running for World Cup qualification with Norway maintaining their four-point lead in the group and Hungary moving ahead of Switzerland into joint second place.
